Sean Gallagher: For route-level A/B testing beta enablement, we need to lock guardrails + alert routing. Right now I’m not seeing a concrete rollback automation hook or a runbook that Support/Oncall can follow.

Sean Gallagher: Proposed minimum guardrails (v1):
- latency regression: p95 +10% vs control OR +75ms (whichever is larger)
- TTFT: p95 +15% vs control OR +100ms
- error rate (5xx + timeouts): +0.25% absolute vs control
- 429s: +0.5% absolute vs control (this one is important w/ capacity constraints)
- optional: if variant error rate > 2% absolute for 5 min, immediate rollback regardless of control

Sean Gallagher: Alert routing proposal:
- guardrail breach (warning) -> #eng-sre + owner channel ping
- guardrail breach (rollback executed) -> #eng-sre + PagerDuty (Inference Platform) if rollback fails or still red 10m after

Sean Gallagher: Questions:
1) Can we confirm where the guardrail evaluator runs (control-plane job vs gateway) and what the hook is to trigger rollback?
2) Who owns the runbook + what’s the URL going to be?

Allison Grant: +1 on needing explicit thresholds + routing. Also need to be careful about small N. If we page on 12 requests we’ll die :)

Allison Grant: Can we add minimum exposure thresholds before guardrails are “armed”? e.g. min 500 exposures per variant AND at least 10 min runtime, otherwise only show as “insufficient data” and no paging.

Miles Thornton: For multi-region, do we evaluate per-region or global? If it’s global-only we can mask one region going bad until it’s too late.

Miles Thornton: Suggest:
- evaluate per region for Hosted
- for Dedicated: per cluster/pool (or whatever the routing boundary is)
- only roll back in the scope that’s impacted, if possible

Dylan Brooks: We were assuming global evaluation for v1 because of complexity, but I’m open to per-region if the dimensions are already in metrics.

Logan Wright: We do have region dimension in the experiment metrics schema, but we’ve been trying to keep cardinality tight. If we do per-region alerts, we should restrict to region as the ONLY additional slice, no route_id/user_id/etc.

Aisha Bello: Agree. Region is fine; anything beyond that gets scary fast. Also we’ll need a default dashboard + alert template keyed on experiment_id + variant_id + region.

Jada Williams: Re: “hook to trigger rollback” — the plan in ENG is:
- guardrail evaluator runs in control-plane (scheduled evaluator every 60s)
- if breach: call Console backend “rollback experiment” endpoint (same path as manual rollback), with reason=guardrail
- emits audit event + posts to Slack via ops webhook

Jada Williams: We haven’t wired the auto-rollback call yet (it’s in my branch). Can we align on the API contract + required fields?

Sean Gallagher: That’s exactly what I want. Rollback automation should use the same audited pathway as a human click.

Sean Gallagher: Required behaviors for auto-rollback:
- idempotent (don’t spam rollback calls)
- cool-down: once rollback triggered, don’t re-trigger for N minutes
- post a single summary message w/ key metrics + link to dashboard
- if rollback fails, page oncall

Amara Diallo: FYI from gateway side: we can tag exposure events with experiment_id, variant_id, region, route_key. route_key is already normalized (not raw URL), so ok.

Nadia Rahman: For cost guardrails: do we want anything for $/req or tokens/req? I’m nervous about paging on cost because it’s noisy, but maybe we at least show it in the rollback message.

Allison Grant: I’d keep cost guardrails out of paging for beta. But in the Slack notification we can include “cost delta” as FYI.

Miles Thornton: +1. Latency/errors are reliability; cost is product/finance.

Dylan Brooks: OK with that. For beta we’ll do reliability guardrails only. We can add cost thresholds later behind config.

Sean Gallagher: Also need explicit precedence: experiments should not override fallbacks in an outage scenario. If fallback policy kicks in (e.g., region degraded), experiment should be suspended or auto-stopped.

Jada Williams: Precedence is being handled in policy engine (experiment assignment happens after route eligibility + before fallback, but fallback can still override on hard failures). We can add a signal to the evaluator: if fallback_override_rate > X%, mark experiment “invalid” and stop.

Logan Wright: We can compute fallback_override_rate from gateway events (we emit fallback_reason). Might take a week to plumb cleanly.

Sean Gallagher: For beta, fine to start with: if error-rate guardrail breach triggers rollback, we’re covered. Let’s not block beta on fallback_override_rate, but add a follow-up.

Allison Grant: Back to alert routing:
- Warnings to #eng-sre + tag experiment owner (we can store owner in experiment config?)
- Criticals: page Inference Platform oncall only if auto-rollback fails OR error-rate is extreme (>2% absolute) for >5 minutes.

Aisha Bello: Owner field exists in Console? If not, could route to #eng-platform-oncall? But that’s noisy.

Dylan Brooks: We can add “created_by” and “last_modified_by” in config but not a durable “owner”. Maybe for beta we require an “experiment contact” field (email/Slack handle) in the experiment config.

Sean Gallagher: Yes. Make it mandatory for beta.

PagerDuty: [PagerDuty] Service “Inference Platform” updated: added new integration key for “ab-guardrails”. (by Allison Grant)

Allison Grant: I’ll set up alert rules + PD routing once the metric names are final. Please don’t rename them after Friday :)

Jada Williams: Metric names from current plan:
- redwood.experiments.latency_ms{stat=p95,experiment_id,variant_id,region}
- redwood.experiments.ttft_ms{stat=p95,...}
- redwood.experiments.error_rate{code_class=5xx|timeout,...}
- redwood.experiments.http_429_rate{...}

Logan Wright: Confirming those are consistent with the schema doc. We’ll also have exposure_count so we can gate alerting.

Miles Thornton: Can the evaluator use a rolling window (5m) + compare to control window, not absolute? Comparing to “control” is crucial because baseline shifts during incidents.

Sean Gallagher: Yes. Rolling 5m windows. And second condition: if control is also bad, don’t rollback just because everything is on fire. We only rollback when variant is worse than control by the deltas.

Jada Williams: Got it. Implementation detail: we’ll compute delta = variant_metric - control_metric and compare against thresholds.

Nadia Rahman: For 429s, use absolute delta? (e.g., 0.5% absolute) feels right.

Allison Grant: Yep. Absolute is easier to reason about.

Sean Gallagher: Action items:
- Jada: wire auto-rollback hook to Console rollback endpoint + add idempotency/cooldown (target this week)
- Allison/Aisha: draft alert rules + PD routing; include min exposures gating
- Dylan: add “experiment contact” required field for beta
- Sean: write runbook (disable/rollback/verify) + link it from the alert message template

Sean Gallagher: Runbook should cover:
1) how to manually stop/rollback in Console
2) how to verify traffic split returned to baseline
3) where to check dashboards (latency/error/429)
4) how to confirm audit log entry
5) comms template for Support/CS

Dylan Brooks: Works. I’ll sync with Tessa/Kenji on copy so “stop” vs “rollback” is not confusing.

Allison Grant: Please include in the runbook: what to do if metrics are “insufficient data” but customer is screaming. (Answer is: rollback anyway.)

Sean Gallagher: lol yes, adding.

Miles Thornton: :thumbsup: + please include region-scoped rollback guidance if available.

Jada Williams: We don’t have region-scoped rollback in v1. Rollback is per experiment (global). We can note that limitation.

Sean Gallagher: Noted. For beta, global rollback is acceptable, but we should call it out explicitly.

Aisha Bello: Once the runbook doc exists, drop link here and I’ll wire it into the Grafana panel + alert annotations.

Sean Gallagher: Will do. Thanks all.
